questions.q: During a migration assessment, a company finds a legacy reporting application that no one has used for nine months and whose data is already duplicated in the data warehouse. Which migration strategy fits?
questions.hint: Unused and redundant: what do you do with something nobody needs?
questions.explanation: Retire means you decommission apps that are unused or redundant. Retain (the main distractor) keeps an app on premises for now, which only makes sense if it's still needed.

questions.q: A company wants to make sure its cloud workloads are run at agreed service levels, with mature monitoring, incident and problem management, and capacity planning. Which AWS CAF perspective covers this?
questions.hint: Think 'running' the workloads day to day, not building them.
questions.explanation: The Operations perspective covers observability, incident and problem management, and capacity so workloads meet SLAs. Platform is about building the cloud environment and architecture.

questions.q: An IAM user is in a group whose policy allows s3:*. A policy attached directly to the user explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject on bucket 'reports'. What happens when the user tries to delete an object in 'reports'?
options: Allowed, because group policies are evaluated first
Denied, because an explicit deny overrides any allow
Allowed, because the most permissive policy wins
Denied only if the user did not sign in with MFA
questions.hint: IAM evaluation has one rule that always wins.
questions.explanation: In IAM policy evaluation an explicit deny always overrides any allow, wherever either one is attached. Nothing picks the 'most permissive' policy.

questions.q: A company must continuously check whether all EBS volumes are encrypted, keep a history of resource configuration changes, and fix noncompliant resources automatically. Which service should it use?
questions.hint: Resource configuration state and compliance, not API activity.
questions.explanation: AWS Config records configuration history, evaluates rules continuously, and can run SSM remediation automatically. CloudTrail logs API calls (who did what), not resource compliance state.

questions.q: Auditors in a central security account need read-only access to resources in 20 member accounts of an AWS Organization. The company does not want to create IAM users in each account. What is the recommended approach?
options: Share each member account's root credentials with the auditors
Create an IAM role in each member account that trusts the security account, and have auditors assume it through AWS STS
Store long-term access keys for each account in AWS Secrets Manager
Add resource-based policies to every S3 bucket
questions.explanation: Cross-account IAM roles assumed through STS give temporary, least-privilege access without creating users. Long-term keys and shared root credentials go against best practice.

questions.q: An order-processing flow must validate payment, reserve inventory, wait for a human approval step, then ship. It needs retries, error branches, and a visual view of each execution's state. Which service fits best?
questions.hint: You need an orchestrator that keeps state between steps.
questions.explanation: Step Functions runs stateful workflows with retries, catch branches, wait-for-callback steps (human approval), and a visual execution history. EventBridge routes events but doesn't keep track of where a workflow is.

questions.q: A company has 40 VPCs across several accounts plus site-to-site VPN connections to on premises. Its full mesh of VPC peering connections has become hard to manage. Which service makes the network topology simpler?
questions.hint: Hub-and-spoke instead of a full mesh.
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway acts as a regional hub that connects many VPCs and VPNs in one place, so you don't need N×(N−1)/2 peering connections. PrivateLink exposes individual services privately but doesn't route between networks.

questions.q: A fraud-detection team needs to query multi-hop relationships between accounts, devices, IP addresses, and transactions with low latency. Which database should it use?
questions.hint: Relationships between entities are the main data here.
questions.explanation: Neptune is a managed graph database built for traversing highly connected data, and fraud rings are a classic graph use case. DocumentDB stores JSON documents and is poor at deep relationship traversal.

questions.q: A company is bringing its own licenses to AWS, and they are licensed per physical socket or core. It needs visibility into the underlying sockets and cores, and control over instance placement, to stay compliant. Which EC2 option fits?
questions.hint: You need the whole physical server, visible to you.
questions.explanation: Dedicated Hosts give you a full physical server with visibility into sockets and cores and control over placement, which per-socket/core BYOL requires. Dedicated Instances isolate hardware but give no socket/core visibility or host control.

questions.q: Finance wants to be alerted automatically to unusual spending spikes, with a root-cause breakdown, without setting fixed dollar thresholds for every service. Which tool should it use?
questions.hint: No fixed thresholds means ML has to learn what normal looks like.
questions.explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn your normal spending, flags anomalies, and shows root causes. Budgets only alerts on thresholds you set yourself.
